messages:
IncBot: :rotating_light: Alert: surge in DNS resolver failures reported from multiple EU POPs (primarily eu-west-2 and eu-central-1) starting now. Upstream lookup error rate ~13% (rolling 5m).

Tara Nguyen: I'm on-call, taking lead. Ethan, plz collect edge logs + synth probe outputs and start customer-impact list.

Ethan Morris: pulling probes now. Quick dig from eu-edge-11: 
```
$ dig @10.20.5.3 api.redwood.com +short
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 35512
```
And curl to front-door returns 502 with log note "dns_lookup_error".

Lena Ivanov: sample edge log: 
```
[2026-03-15T23:10:02Z] eu-edge-11 resolver=10.20.5.3 q=generate.v2.redwood status=SERVFAIL attempts=2
[2026-03-15T23:10:03Z] eu-edge-14 upstream=frontend-4 status=502 note="dns_lookup_error"
```

Ricardo Silva: CS Ops, please start the customer sweep. Prioritize EU prod customers and any Dedicated deployments.

CS Ops: acknowledged. pulling list; will DM CSMs and open tickets for impacted orgs.

Tara Nguyen: initial hypothesis: intermittent external resolver/provider issue (Cloudflare/Route53) or a peering path flap. Mitigations to consider: A) prepend global multi-provider resolvers in edge config B) update Route53 geo policy to failover EU to fallback resolver pool C) enable TCP-first or increase DNS retries D) short circuit cache for critical prefixes. I'd vote for A+B fast, plus C if we still see issues.

Ethan Morris: agree A+B first. I'm prepping edge config change to add fallback resolvers and set resolver_order=[multi,local]. Will run rolling 3-node concurrency.

Edge Agent Bot: dry-run for config change passed on eu fleets. Ready to deploy.

Tara Nguyen: Ricardo, can you stage weighted Route53 update to bias EU queries to our fallback pool at 70%? We'll keep 30% on primary to keep diagnostics.

Ricardo Silva: preparing change file: 
```
cat > /tmp/route53-eu-failover.json <<EOF
{ "Comment": "failover eu to fallback pool 70%", "Changes": [...] }
EOF
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZRWD333 --change-batch file:///tmp/route53-eu-failover.json
```
Submitted change. Change ID: CHG-223-FA1L.

Ethan Morris: rolling edge change now: 
```
/opt/edgectl rollout --region eu --change resolver.prepend=203.0.113.10,198.51.100.20 --concurrency 3
```

Edge Agent Bot: rollout progress: 6/18 nodes updated; health checks passing.

CS Ops: customers affected (initial): NorthernRetail-EU, DataSync EU-prod, Integra Labs EU. Notifying all, tickets opened.

Tara Nguyen: vendor outreach: opening tickets with Cloudflare and AWS Route53. Provide probes + timelines. Lena, can you attach traceroutes and pcap snippets?

Lena Ivanov: attaching traceroute: 
```
traceroute to 203.0.113.10 (203.0.113.10), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  1.1 ms  1.0 ms  0.9 ms
 2  198.51.100.1  10.2 ms  10.5 ms  10.7 ms
 3  * * *
 4  203.0.113.34  23.1 ms  23.0 ms  23.3 ms
```

Cloudflare Support: (auto-reply) ticket received. Please include sample logs and timestamps. We're checking POP health for eu-west-2.

Route53 Support: (auto-reply) we've received your case. Routing & query logs requested.

Ethan Morris: after first half of rollout, resolver failures dropped from 13% -> 4.6% in EU. Some spikes persist in eu-west-2.

Tara Nguyen: good improvement. Keep rollout going. Ricardo, any ETA on Route53 change propagation?

Ricardo Silva: AWS change acknowledged; geo policy changes generally reflected in ~30-90s; our monitoring should pick it up.

Edge Agent Bot: rollout complete (18/18 nodes). All eu edges now use multi-provider fallback as primary. Health checks show 98% success on DNS synths.

CS Ops: updating customers: most report recovered. Keeping tickets open for those who still see intermittent failures.

Lena Ivanov: vendor update: Cloudflare flagged increased query timeouts on a subset of their EU resolvers between 23:08-23:14 UTC due to an internal load/peering event; they are engineering a mitigation. Route53 noticed elevated NX/TCP retries correlated with same window.

Tara Nguyen: until vendors confirm, we'll keep Route53 bias in place for 1 hour and maintain multi-resolver edge config. Also create follow-ups: 1) increase synthetic DNS probes across EU POPs, 2) add automated failover trigger when SERVFAIL > 5% for 2m, 3) evaluate adding a third resolver provider in EU, 4) revisit TTLs for critical records. Owners: Ethan (edge), Lena (network/vendor), Ricardo (dns routing), CS Ops (customer comms).

Ethan Morris: flipping on TCP-first on edges now as extra protection: 
```
/opt/edgectl set resolver.tcp_first=true --region eu --concurrency 4
```
Deployed. Expected CPU/network overhead minor; monitoring CPU.

CS Ops: customers still reporting minor latency: NorthernRetail-EU reporting slower lookup time but no errors. Notifying them of mitigation steps and expected timeline.

Tara Nguyen: handing off to Ricardo for next pager period. I'll remain reachable for escalation. Please capture all logs and add to incident doc.

Ricardo Silva: taking handoff. Keeping Route53 bias in place. Monitoring at 30s synth cadence.

Cloudflare Support: update: mitigation deployed to affected EU POPs; error rates returning to baseline. Monitoring continues.

Route53 Support: update: query retry spikes subsided after CF mitigation; logs show reduced TCP retries to resolver pool. Recommending gradual revert only after stable 1 hour.

Ricardo Silva: current EU error rate ~0.9%. Leaving failover for 60 minutes then canary revert 10% every 10 minutes if stable.

CS Ops: customer follow-up scheduled for when we finalize revert. Postmortem requested.

Tara Nguyen: post-incident: plan a runbook update to automate (A) edge-prepend on DNS failure, (B) Route53 quick-failover play, (C) customer notification template. Also assess cost/perf of adding third provider.

IncBot: Incident update  Mitigation applied; partial recovery confirmed. Continue monitoring and add any remaining logs to the incident document.
